Prefer per-workload cloud identity over node-level credentials
Use a CNI that enforces NetworkPolicy (Calico, Cilium) — policies are silently ignored otherwise
Default-deny ingress AND egress in every namespace, then allow-list explicitly
Explicitly deny pod traffic to the control plane and etcd
Restrict who can create LoadBalancer / externalIPs Services — enable DenyServiceExternalIPs (CVE-2020-8554 traffic interception)
Mount Secrets as files, not environment variables — env vars leak via crash dumps, logs, and /proc
Prefer an external secret store (Vault, cloud secret manager) over raw etcd Secrets
Scope Secret access with resourceNames so a workload reads only its own
Rotate any secret exposed to a compromised namespace; assume disclosure
Pull only from trusted/private registries; block public registries via admission policy
Pin image digests (not :latest) so the running image cannot change underneath you
Scan images for vulnerabilities and fail builds on critical findings
Enforce image signatures at admission (Sigstore/Cosign, Kyverno, or equivalent)
Enforce policy at admission with ValidatingAdmissionPolicy, Kyverno, or OPA/Gatekeeper
Fail closed — a webhook that fails open is not a control
Restrict who can modify admission webhooks; editing them disables every policy at once
Separate sensitive workloads onto dedicated nodes (taints/affinity) so a container escape does not land next to secrets-bearing pods
Isolate tenants by namespace + node pool; use separate clusters for hostile multi-tenancy
Set CPU/memory limits and enforce with ResourceQuota/LimitRange — unbounded pods are a cheap DoS
Patch node OS and container runtime on a schedule
Enable API server audit logging and ship it off-cluster — an attacker with cluster-admin can erase local logs
Alert on: system:masters use, new ClusterRoleBindings, exec into pods, Secret reads by unusual identities, failed auth spikes
Deploy runtime detection (Falco or equivalent) for escape and crypto-mining behaviour
Rehearse credential revocation: rotate tokens, certs, and cloud keys reachable from the cluster

guides.title: LangChain Configuration
checklistItems: Upgrade Every LangChain Package to a Patched Release - pass: pip-audit reports no known vulnerabilities in the installed LangChain packages
Pin and Patch the Checkpoint and Store Packages Separately - pass: langgraph-checkpoint and its Postgres and SQLite backends are pinned to their current patched releases
Rebuild the Agent Server Image on a Patched Release - pass: the deployed agent image carries the latest langgraph-api release
Upgrade the Tracing SDK to a Patched Release - pass: langsmith is at its latest release
Require Package Hashes on Every Install - pass: requirements.txt carries --hash= for every package and the image installs with --require-hashes

Pin langchain-community to Its Final Release and Schedule Its Removal (archived by the vendor, no further security fixes; move each integration to its partner package) - pass: langchain-community is pinned to its final release and a dated ticket tracks moving each integration to its partner package

Uninstall langchain-experimental (archived by the vendor, no further fixes; it ships the in-process PythonREPLTool and PALChain) - pass: langchain-experimental is not installed and not listed in any requirements file
Upgrade the JavaScript Packages to Patched Releases - pass: npm audit reports no vulnerabilities in the LangChain JavaScript packages
Make the Advisory Scan Fail the Build - pass: the CI pipeline runs pip-audit and npm audit --audit-level=high as blocking steps
Set Every allow_dangerous_ Opt-In to False (each opt-in lets the agent load pickled objects or fetch arbitrary URLs) - pass: no allow_dangerous_*=True remains in the repository

Replace In-Process Code Execution with a Container-Sandboxed Shell Tool (PythonREPLTool, PALChain and ShellTool run agent-written code inside the server process; the default host policy sandboxes nothing) - pass: no in-process code tool is imported and every shell tool uses a container execution policy
Grant Tool Credentials Read-Only Access Wherever the Task Allows - pass: every database credential a tool holds can only SELECT unless the task needs writes
Require Human Approval Before an Irreversible Tool Runs - pass: every tool that sends, deletes, pays or deploys is listed in a HumanInTheLoopMiddleware interrupt_on map
Set Tool and Model Call Limits - pass: every agent runs with ToolCallLimitMiddleware and ModelCallLimitMiddleware and explicit run limits
Review Every Public Prompt-Hub Pull and Replace It with a Prompt You Own - pass: no agent pulls a public hub prompt at runtime; every prompt lives in a workspace you own
Configure Custom Authentication - pass: auth.path in langgraph.json points at your authentication handler
Do Not Turn Off Authentication for Studio Requests - pass: auth.disable_studio_auth is false or absent
Restrict CORS Origins to an Explicit List - pass: http.cors.allow_origins lists only your application origins
Disable Unused Endpoints - pass: every endpoint group the agent does not use (mcp, a2a, ui, meta, store) is disabled
Enable Authentication on Custom Routes and Run It First - pass: http.enable_custom_route_auth is true and http.middleware_order is auth_first
Exclude Credentials from Header Logging - pass: http.logging_headers.excludes lists authorization, cookie and x-api-key
Do Not Enable the LangSmith API-Key Fallback - pass: auth.allow_langsmith_api_keys is false or absent
Set Checkpoint and Store TTLs - pass: checkpointer.ttl and store.ttl set a default_ttl no longer than your retention policy
Disable the Pickle Fallback and Set an Explicit JSON Module Allowlist - pass: checkpointer.serde.pickle_fallback is false and allowed_json_modules lists only the classes the state needs
Restrict Webhook Targets in the URL Policy - pass: webhooks.url allows only your domains over HTTPS on port 443 and blocks private IPs
Encrypt Checkpoints at Rest - pass: LANGGRAPH_AES_KEY is set on the Agent Server from a secret and is 32 hex characters
Disable Tracing or Point It at an Instance You Govern - pass: LANGSMITH_TRACING is false, or LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT is a LangSmith instance you operate or contractually govern
Hide Inputs and Outputs When Traces Leave the Boundary - pass: LANGSMITH_HIDE_INPUTS and LANGSMITH_HIDE_OUTPUTS are true whenever traces go to an external instance
Set a Trace Sampling Rate - pass: LANGSMITH_TRACING_SAMPLING_RATE is set below 1 in production
Restrict Standalone-Server Egress to an Allowlist - pass: the agent's egress NetworkPolicy allows the trace endpoint on 443 and nothing else beyond the model and checkpoint endpoints
Connect to MCP Servers Over HTTPS Only, with an Explicit Credential - pass: every MCP client URL is https:// and carries an explicit auth credential
Require Approval for MCP Tools Annotated Destructive, Not by Tool Name - pass: the interrupt policy keys on the MCP destructiveHint annotation rather than a list of tool names
Send Each User's Own Credential on MCP Calls, Never One Shared Token - pass: MCP calls carry the requesting user's token, and no shared static token is configured

Deny All Egress by Default and Allow Only the Model, Checkpoint and Trace Endpoints - pass: a NetworkPolicy selecting the agent pods denies egress by default and allows only the model, checkpoint and trace endpoints
Block the Metadata Endpoint - pass: the egress policy excludes 169.254.169.254/32
Disable Service-Account Token Automount - pass: the agent's service account has automountServiceAccountToken: false
Run the Agent Non-Root with a Read-Only Root Filesystem - pass: the agent pod has runAsNonRoot: true, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true and allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
Move Any Provider Key Found in the Repository or Image to a Secret Manager and Rotate It - pass: no provider or LangSmith key appears in the repository or image, and every key found was rotated

items.title: Upgrade Every LangChain Package to a Patched Release
items.pass: `pip-audit` reports no known vulnerabilities in the installed LangChain packages

fix: pip install pip-audit && pip-audit -r requirements.txt --fix && pip install -r requirements.txt
cli.expect: `No known vulnerabilities found`. Every advisory listed is a public exploit path into the agent process.

items.title: Pin and Patch the Checkpoint and Store Packages Separately
items.pass: `langgraph-checkpoint` and its Postgres and SQLite backends are pinned to their current patched releases

fix:
pip install pip-tools && pip-compile -P langgraph-checkpoint -P langgraph-checkpoint-postgres \
  -P langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite -o requirements.txt requirements.in && pip install -r requirements.txt
cli.expect: each package prints a `Version` equal to the latest release on PyPI. The checkpoint packages deserialize stored state, so an old one is a deserialization bug waiting for a crafted checkpoint.

items.title: Rebuild the Agent Server Image on a Patched Release
items.pass: the deployed agent image carries the latest `langgraph-api` release

cli.expect: `Version` equals the latest `langgraph-api` release. The server package is the HTTP surface of the agent, and an old image keeps every fixed server bug live.

items.title: Upgrade the Tracing SDK to a Patched Release
items.pass: `langsmith` is at its latest release

cli.expect: `Version` equals the latest `langsmith` release. The tracing SDK ships prompts and outputs off the host, so a patched client is the one you want handling them.

items.title: Require Package Hashes on Every Install
items.pass: `requirements.txt` carries `--hash=` for every package and the image installs with `--require-hashes`

fix:
pip install pip-tools && pip-compile --generate-hashes -o requirements.txt requirements.in && \
  pip install --require-hashes -r requirements.txt
cli.expect: a `--hash=` line for every requirement and `--require-hashes` in the install command. Without hashes a hijacked package name on the index installs unnoticed.

items.title: Pin langchain-community to Its Final Release and Schedule Its Removal (archived by the vendor, no further security fixes; move each integration to its partner package)
items.pass: `langchain-community` is pinned to its final release and a dated ticket tracks moving each integration to its partner package

fix:
pip install pip-tools && pip-compile -P langchain-community -o requirements.txt requirements.in && \
  pip install -r requirements.txt
cli.expect: either `not found`, or `Version` equal to the final published release with a removal ticket on the board. An archived package ships no fix for the next advisory.

items.title: Uninstall langchain-experimental (archived by the vendor, no further fixes; it ships the in-process PythonREPLTool and PALChain)
items.pass: `langchain-experimental` is not installed and not listed in any requirements file

fix: pip uninstall -y langchain-experimental && sed -i '/^langchain-experimental/d' requirements.in requirements.txt
cli.expect: `WARNING: Package(s) not found: langchain-experimental`. The package puts an unsandboxed Python REPL one import away from every agent.

items.title: Upgrade the JavaScript Packages to Patched Releases
items.pass: `npm audit` reports no vulnerabilities in the LangChain JavaScript packages

cli.expect: `found 0 vulnerabilities`. Each listed advisory is a public exploit path into the Node agent.

items.title: Make the Advisory Scan Fail the Build
items.pass: the CI pipeline runs `pip-audit` and `npm audit --audit-level=high` as blocking steps

fix: pip install pip-audit && pip-audit -r requirements.txt && npm audit --audit-level=high
cli.expect: at least one hit in a pipeline step that has no `continue-on-error` or `allow_failure`. A scan that only warns is a scan nobody reads.

items.title: Set Every allow_dangerous_ Opt-In to False (each opt-in lets the agent load pickled objects or fetch arbitrary URLs)
items.pass: no `allow_dangerous_*=True` remains in the repository

cli.expect: no output, or only lines ending in `=False`. Each opt-in lets the agent unpickle attacker-supplied objects or fetch arbitrary URLs from inside the server.

items.title: Replace In-Process Code Execution with a Container-Sandboxed Shell Tool (PythonREPLTool, PALChain and ShellTool run agent-written code inside the server process; the default host policy sandboxes nothing)
items.pass: no in-process code tool is imported and every shell tool uses a container execution policy

cli.expect: no output. An in-process tool runs model-written code with the server's secrets, filesystem and network.

items.title: Grant Tool Credentials Read-Only Access Wherever the Task Allows
items.pass: every database credential a tool holds can only `SELECT` unless the task needs writes

fix:
psql -d <db> -c "CREATE ROLE agent_ro LOGIN PASSWORD '<password>'; GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE <db> TO agent_ro; \
  GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO agent_ro; GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO agent_ro"
cli.expect: `f`. A tool credential that can write turns a prompt injection into a data-destruction path.

items.title: Require Human Approval Before an Irreversible Tool Runs
items.pass: every tool that sends, deletes, pays or deploys is listed in a `HumanInTheLoopMiddleware` `interrupt_on` map

cli.expect: one `interrupt_on` entry naming each irreversible tool. Without an interrupt the model's first mistaken call is final.

items.title: Set Tool and Model Call Limits
items.pass: every agent runs with `ToolCallLimitMiddleware` and `ModelCallLimitMiddleware` and explicit run limits

cli.expect: both middlewares appear in every agent definition with a `run_limit`. An unbounded loop burns budget and keeps retrying a harmful tool call until it succeeds.

items.title: Review Every Public Prompt-Hub Pull and Replace It with a Prompt You Own
items.pass: no agent pulls a public hub prompt at runtime; every prompt lives in a workspace you own

console.verify: LangSmith > Prompts > every prompt the agents load is listed under your workspace, and none is a public prompt from another owner
console.fix: LangSmith > Prompts > open the public prompt > Fork into your workspace > review the text > Commit; then update the agent to pull your copy by name

cli.expect: no `dangerously_pull_public_prompt`, and every `pull_prompt` names a prompt in your own workspace. A public prompt can be edited by its owner at any time and lands in your agent on the next run.

items.title: Configure Custom Authentication
items.pass: `auth.path` in `langgraph.json` points at your authentication handler

fix: jq '.auth.path = "./auth.py:auth"' langgraph.json > langgraph.json.tmp && mv langgraph.json.tmp langgraph.json
cli.expect: `"./auth.py:auth"` or your handler's path, not `null`. Without a handler every request to the server is anonymous.

items.title: Do Not Turn Off Authentication for Studio Requests
items.pass: `auth.disable_studio_auth` is `false` or absent

fix: jq '.auth.disable_studio_auth = false' langgraph.json > langgraph.json.tmp && mv langgraph.json.tmp langgraph.json
cli.expect: `false` or `null`. Disabling it lets any request that claims to come from Studio skip your handler.

items.title: Restrict CORS Origins to an Explicit List
items.pass: `http.cors.allow_origins` lists only your application origins

fix:
jq '.http.cors.allow_origins = ["https://<app-origin>"]' langgraph.json > langgraph.json.tmp && \
  mv langgraph.json.tmp langgraph.json
cli.expect: an array of your own `https://` origins with no `*`. A wildcard lets any web page call the server with the user's cookies.

items.title: Disable Unused Endpoints
items.pass: every endpoint group the agent does not use (`mcp`, `a2a`, `ui`, `meta`, `store`) is disabled

verify: jq '.http | {disable_mcp, disable_a2a, disable_ui, disable_meta, disable_store}' langgraph.json
fix:
jq '.http += {disable_mcp:true, disable_a2a:true, disable_ui:true, disable_meta:true, disable_store:true}' \
  langgraph.json > langgraph.json.tmp && mv langgraph.json.tmp langgraph.json
cli.expect: `true` for every group the agent does not use. Each enabled group is an authenticated surface you are not watching.

items.title: Enable Authentication on Custom Routes and Run It First
items.pass: `http.enable_custom_route_auth` is `true` and `http.middleware_order` is `auth_first`

fix:
jq '.http.enable_custom_route_auth = true | .http.middleware_order = "auth_first"' langgraph.json \
  > langgraph.json.tmp && mv langgraph.json.tmp langgraph.json
cli.expect: `true` then `"auth_first"`. Otherwise custom routes serve unauthenticated, and custom middleware runs before the caller is known.

items.title: Exclude Credentials from Header Logging
items.pass: `http.logging_headers.excludes` lists `authorization`, `cookie` and `x-api-key`

fix:
jq '.http.logging_headers = {excludes: ["authorization", "cookie", "x-api-key"]}' langgraph.json \
  > langgraph.json.tmp && mv langgraph.json.tmp langgraph.json
cli.expect: an `excludes` array containing `authorization`, `cookie` and `x-api-key`. Logged headers put every bearer token and session cookie into the log pipeline.

items.title: Do Not Enable the LangSmith API-Key Fallback
items.pass: `auth.allow_langsmith_api_keys` is `false` or absent

fix: jq '.auth.allow_langsmith_api_keys = false' langgraph.json > langgraph.json.tmp && mv langgraph.json.tmp langgraph.json
cli.expect: `false` or `null`. With the fallback on, any LangSmith API key in the workspace also authenticates to the agent, bypassing your handler.

items.title: Set Checkpoint and Store TTLs
items.pass: `checkpointer.ttl` and `store.ttl` set a `default_ttl` no longer than your retention policy

fix:
jq '.checkpointer.ttl = {strategy:"delete", default_ttl:43200, sweep_interval_minutes:60} |
    .store.ttl = {default_ttl:43200, refresh_on_read:false, sweep_interval_minutes:60}' \
  langgraph.json > langgraph.json.tmp && mv langgraph.json.tmp langgraph.json
cli.expect: both objects present with `default_ttl` in minutes within policy and a `sweep_interval_minutes`. Without a TTL every conversation and its inputs stay in the database forever.

items.title: Disable the Pickle Fallback and Set an Explicit JSON Module Allowlist
items.pass: `checkpointer.serde.pickle_fallback` is `false` and `allowed_json_modules` lists only the classes the state needs

fix:
jq '.checkpointer.serde = {pickle_fallback:false, allowed_json_modules:[["<module>","<Class>"]]}' \
  langgraph.json > langgraph.json.tmp && mv langgraph.json.tmp langgraph.json
cli.expect: `pickle_fallback: false` and an explicit `allowed_json_modules` array. With pickle enabled a crafted checkpoint executes code when it is loaded.

items.title: Restrict Webhook Targets in the URL Policy
items.pass: `webhooks.url` allows only your domains over HTTPS on port 443 and blocks private IPs

fix:
jq '.webhooks.url = {allowed_domains:["hooks.<your-domain>"], require_https:true, disable_private_ips:true, allowed_ports:[443]}' \
  langgraph.json > langgraph.json.tmp && mv langgraph.json.tmp langgraph.json
cli.expect: `allowed_domains` naming your hosts, `require_https: true`, `disable_private_ips: true`, `allowed_ports: [443]`. An open policy lets a run's webhook field point at internal services.

items.title: Encrypt Checkpoints at Rest
items.pass: `LANGGRAPH_AES_KEY` is set on the Agent Server from a secret and is 32 hex characters

verify: kubectl exec deployment/$AGENT -n $NS -- printenv LANGGRAPH_AES_KEY | tr -d '\n' | wc -c
fix:
kubectl create secret generic langgraph-aes -n $NS --from-literal=LANGGRAPH_AES_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) && \
  kubectl set env deployment/$AGENT -n $NS --from=secret/langgraph-aes
cli.expect: `32`. Without the key every checkpoint sits in Postgres in plain text.

items.title: Disable Tracing or Point It at an Instance You Govern
items.pass: `LANGSMITH_TRACING` is `false`, or `LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT` is a LangSmith instance you operate or contractually govern

verify: kubectl exec deployment/$AGENT -n $NS -- printenv LANGSMITH_TRACING LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT
cli.expect: `false`, or `true` followed by the endpoint of your governed instance. Default tracing sends every prompt and output to the vendor's cloud.

items.title: Hide Inputs and Outputs When Traces Leave the Boundary
items.pass: `LANGSMITH_HIDE_INPUTS` and `LANGSMITH_HIDE_OUTPUTS` are `true` whenever traces go to an external instance

verify: kubectl exec deployment/$AGENT -n $NS -- printenv LANGSMITH_HIDE_INPUTS LANGSMITH_HIDE_OUTPUTS
fix: kubectl set env deployment/$AGENT -n $NS LANGSMITH_HIDE_INPUTS=true LANGSMITH_HIDE_OUTPUTS=true
cli.expect: `true` on both lines. Otherwise the full prompt and completion, with whatever customer data they carry, leave the boundary in every trace.

items.title: Set a Trace Sampling Rate
items.pass: `LANGSMITH_TRACING_SAMPLING_RATE` is set below `1` in production

cli.expect: a value such as `0.1`. Full sampling exports every production conversation rather than a debugging sample.

items.title: Restrict Standalone-Server Egress to an Allowlist
items.pass: the agent's egress NetworkPolicy allows the trace endpoint on 443 and nothing else beyond the model and checkpoint endpoints

cli.expect: an egress policy selecting the agent pods, with rules only for the model, checkpoint and trace endpoints. Unrestricted egress lets a prompt injection exfiltrate state to any host.

items.title: Connect to MCP Servers Over HTTPS Only, with an Explicit Credential
items.pass: every MCP client URL is `https://` and carries an explicit auth credential

cli.expect: no MCP server URL in the output. A plain-HTTP MCP connection exposes tool calls and their credentials on the wire.

items.title: Require Approval for MCP Tools Annotated Destructive, Not by Tool Name
items.pass: the interrupt policy keys on the MCP `destructiveHint` annotation rather than a list of tool names

cli.expect: at least one hit inside the approval predicate. A name list misses every destructive tool the MCP server adds or renames later.

items.title: Send Each User's Own Credential on MCP Calls, Never One Shared Token
items.pass: MCP calls carry the requesting user's token, and no shared static token is configured

cli.expect: every MCP client auth derives from the current user, with no hard-coded or environment-wide token. A shared token gives every user the union of everyone's permissions on the MCP server.

items.title: Deny All Egress by Default and Allow Only the Model, Checkpoint and Trace Endpoints
items.pass: a NetworkPolicy selecting the agent pods denies egress by default and allows only the model, checkpoint and trace endpoints

cli.expect: a policy with `policyTypes: [Egress]` selecting the agent pods and `egress` rules only for the three endpoint sets. Without it the agent can reach every service in the cluster and on the internet.

items.title: Block the Metadata Endpoint
items.pass: the egress policy excludes `169.254.169.254/32`

cli.expect: the address appears under an `except` list. Reaching the metadata endpoint hands the agent the node's cloud credentials.

items.title: Disable Service-Account Token Automount
items.pass: the agent's service account has `automountServiceAccountToken: false`

cli.expect: `false` for the agent's service account. A mounted token lets code the agent runs talk to the Kubernetes API as the pod.

items.title: Run the Agent Non-Root with a Read-Only Root Filesystem
items.pass: the agent pod has `runAsNonRoot: true`, `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` and `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`

cli.expect: `readOnlyRootFilesystem:true` and `allowPrivilegeEscalation:false` on every agent container, with `runAsNonRoot:true` on the pod. A root, writable container turns any code-execution bug into a full host foothold.

items.title: Move Any Provider Key Found in the Repository or Image to a Secret Manager and Rotate It
items.pass: no provider or LangSmith key appears in the repository or image, and every key found was rotated

fix:
kubectl create secret generic provider-keys -n $NS --from-literal=OPENAI_API_KEY=<rotated-key> \
  --from-literal=LANGSMITH_API_KEY=<rotated-key> && kubectl set env deployment/$AGENT -n $NS --from=secret/provider-keys
cli.expect: no output. A key in git history or an image layer is already shared with everyone who can pull either.

guides.title: Langfuse Configuration
checklistItems: Assign Organization Roles at Least Privilege - pass: every organization member holds the lowest role their work needs, and only the named owners hold OWNER

Set Single-Project Users to NONE Plus a Project Role (the organization role NONE is set under Organization Settings > Members; the memberships API takes OWNER, ADMIN, MEMBER or VIEWER) - pass: a user who works in one project holds organization role NONE and a role on that project only
Set a Data Retention Window - pass: every project has Data Retention set to a day count no larger than your policy allows, not disabled
Review Project API Keys and Rotate Them on a Schedule - pass: every project API key has a note naming its service and environment and was created inside your rotation window
Revoke Organization-Scoped API Keys Not Used for Provisioning - pass: the only organization API keys are the ones your provisioning automation holds
Restrict Stored LLM Connections to Approved Endpoints - pass: every LLM connection's base URL is an approved provider or gateway
Unshare Public Traces That Are Not Safe to Publish - pass: no trace is public unless it was reviewed for publication
Enforce Enterprise SSO for Your Verified Domain (Cloud) - pass: the corporate domain is verified and its SSO connection is set to Enforced
Review Audit Logs on a Schedule - pass: an owner reviews the organization audit log at least monthly and records the review

Provision and Deprovision Users Through SCIM (point the IdP's SCIM provisioning at /api/public/scim with an organization key; the delete below is the offboarding step) - pass: membership is managed by the IdP's SCIM connector and no offboarded person remains in SCIM Users
Sign Up in the Cloud Data Region Your Residency Policy Allows - pass: the organization lives on the region host your residency policy allows and every SDK points at that host
Do Not Enable AI Features Until Approved - pass: Enable AI powered features for your organization is Off unless security approved it
Turn Off AI Data Use for Product Improvement - pass: AI Data Use for Product/Service Improvement is Off
Protect the Production Prompt Label - pass: production and every label an application resolves are protected labels
Disconnect Any Slack Workspace You Do Not Control - pass: the Slack integration is disconnected or connected only to your own workspace
Review and Remove Unnecessary or Unrecognized Integrations - pass: every integration (Slack, PostHog, blob storage export) is one your team set up on purpose
Send Webhook Credentials in Headers, Never in the URL - pass: every prompt automation webhook carries its token in a header and its URL has no secret in the query string

Generate a Unique NEXTAUTH_SECRET, SALT and ENCRYPTION_KEY per Environment at Install (rotating SALT breaks every API key; rotating ENCRYPTION_KEY makes stored credentials unreadable) - pass: each environment has its own random NEXTAUTH_SECRET, SALT and 64-hex-character ENCRYPTION_KEY

Remove the Bootstrap Secrets After First Start (the init values are applied once; afterwards they only sit in the environment as live secrets) - pass: no LANGFUSE_INIT_USER_PASSWORD, LANGFUSE_INIT_PROJECT_SECRET_KEY or LANGFUSE_INIT_PROJECT_PUBLIC_KEY is set on web or worker
Set Data Retention at Provisioning - pass: LANGFUSE_INIT_PROJECT_RETENTION is set to the day count your policy allows and the bootstrap project shows that retention
Disable Open Sign-Up - pass: AUTH_DISABLE_SIGNUP is true on the web deployment
Disable Email/Password When SSO Covers Everyone - pass: AUTH_DISABLE_USERNAME_PASSWORD is true once every user signs in through SSO
Force SSO for Corporate Domains - pass: AUTH_DOMAINS_WITH_SSO_ENFORCEMENT lists every corporate email domain
Require Email Verification Where Password Auth Remains - pass: AUTH_EMAIL_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED is true wherever password login is still enabled
Shorten the Session Lifetime - pass: AUTH_SESSION_MAX_AGE is set to the number of minutes your policy allows
Do Not Enable Account Linking Unless the IdP Verifies Emails - pass: no AUTH_<PROVIDER>_ALLOW_ACCOUNT_LINKING is true for a provider that does not verify email addresses
Pin the SSO Issuer - pass: every configured SSO provider has AUTH_<PROVIDER>_ISSUER set to your IdP's issuer URL
Set Explicit OAuth Checks on Every SSO Provider - pass: every configured SSO provider has AUTH_<PROVIDER>_CHECKS=pkce,state
Limit Google Sign-In to Corporate Domains - pass: AUTH_GOOGLE_ALLOWED_DOMAINS lists only your corporate domains when Google sign-in is enabled
Restrict Who Can Create Organizations - pass: LANGFUSE_ALLOWED_ORGANIZATION_CREATORS lists only the owners' addresses
Set the Auto-Provisioned Default Roles to VIEWER - pass: LANGFUSE_DEFAULT_ORG_ROLE and LANGFUSE_DEFAULT_PROJECT_ROLE are VIEWER
Set a Server-Side Masking Callback - pass: LANGFUSE_INGESTION_MASKING_CALLBACK_URL points at your masking service on both web and worker
Set Masking to Fail Closed - pass: LANGFUSE_INGESTION_MASKING_CALLBACK_FAIL_CLOSED is true on both web and worker
Close the Legacy Ingestion Endpoint - pass: LANGFUSE_MIGRATION_V4_WRITE_MODE is unset once every SDK is on the current ingestion path
Enforce HTTPS at the CSP Layer - pass: LANGFUSE_CSP_ENFORCE_HTTPS is true on the web deployment
Turn Off Telemetry (OSS) - pass: TELEMETRY_ENABLED is false on web and worker
Do Not Set SSRF Allowlists Unless an Internal Target Is Required - pass: no LANGFUSE_WHITELISTED variable is set unless a documented internal target needs it
Never Run Code Evaluators In-Process - pass: LANGFUSE_CODE_EVAL_DISPATCHER is unset or set to a sandboxed dispatcher
Generate a High-Entropy Admin API Key and Do Not Expose the Admin API Publicly - pass: ADMIN_API_KEY is at least 64 random characters and /api/admin is blocked at the ingress

Sandbox or Disable the Assistant's Code Tools (or set LANGFUSE_IN_APP_AGENT_ENABLED=false) - pass: the in-app agent is disabled, or its sandbox provider is lambda-microvm with image, role, region and egress connector set
Expose Only the Web Container - pass: langfuse-web is the only Service of type LoadBalancer or NodePort in the namespace
Enable Encryption at Rest on Every Store - pass: every bucket Langfuse writes to has default SSE-KMS encryption, and the database volumes are encrypted
Grant the Retention Job Delete Rights on Every Bucket - pass: the Langfuse role can s3:DeleteObject on the event, media and export buckets
Upgrade the Instance to the Latest Release - pass: web and worker run the image tag of the latest Langfuse release

items.title: Assign Organization Roles at Least Privilege
items.pass: every organization member holds the lowest role their work needs, and only the named owners hold `OWNER`

console.verify: Organization Settings > Members > Role column shows `OWNER` only for the named owners and `ADMIN`, `MEMBER` or `VIEWER` for everyone else
console.fix: Organization Settings > Members > select the member > Role > choose the lowest role that fits > Save

cli.expect: `memberships` lists `"role":"OWNER"` only for the named owners. An extra owner can delete the organization and every project in it.

items.title: Set Single-Project Users to NONE Plus a Project Role (the organization role NONE is set under Organization Settings > Members; the memberships API takes OWNER, ADMIN, MEMBER or VIEWER)
items.pass: a user who works in one project holds organization role `NONE` and a role on that project only

console.verify: Organization Settings > Members > single-project users show Organization Role `NONE` and one entry under Project Roles
console.fix: Organization Settings > Members > select the user > Organization Role > `NONE` > Save; then Project Settings > Members > Add member > choose the user > role `MEMBER` or `VIEWER` > Add

cli.expect: every single-project user is listed with `"role":"NONE"` at the organization level. An organization-level `MEMBER` reaches every project in the organization, including ones the user was never meant to see.

items.title: Set a Data Retention Window
items.pass: every project has Data Retention set to a day count no larger than your policy allows, not disabled

console.verify: Project Settings > General > Data Retention shows a number of days within your policy, not disabled
console.fix: Project Settings > General > Data Retention > enter the number of days > Save

cli.expect: each project's `retentionDays` is a number within your policy, not `0` or absent. Traces kept forever hold prompts and outputs with customer data long after anyone needs them.

items.title: Review Project API Keys and Rotate Them on a Schedule
items.pass: every project API key has a note naming its service and environment and was created inside your rotation window

console.verify: Project Settings > API Keys > every key shows a note naming a service and environment and a Created date inside the rotation window
console.fix: Project Settings > API Keys > Create new API key > Note `<service>-<environment>-<date>` > Create > store the secret in the service's secret manager; then Project Settings > API Keys > select the old key > Delete > confirm

cli.expect: every key's `note` names a service and environment and its `createdAt` is inside the rotation window. A key nobody can attribute cannot be revoked with confidence when it leaks.

items.title: Revoke Organization-Scoped API Keys Not Used for Provisioning
items.pass: the only organization API keys are the ones your provisioning automation holds

console.verify: Organization Settings > API Keys > every key's note names a provisioning system (IdP SCIM, Terraform, CI)
console.fix: Organization Settings > API Keys > select the key > Delete > confirm

cli.expect: `apiKeys` lists only keys whose `note` names a provisioning system. An organization key can create projects, members and keys across the whole organization.

items.title: Restrict Stored LLM Connections to Approved Endpoints
items.pass: every LLM connection's base URL is an approved provider or gateway

console.verify: Project Settings > LLM Connections > each connection's API Base URL is empty (provider default) or an approved gateway
console.fix: Project Settings > LLM Connections > select the connection > Edit > API Base URL > enter the approved gateway URL > Save; delete any connection nobody approved

cli.expect: every entry's `baseURL` is null or an approved endpoint. A connection to an unknown host sends prompts, outputs and the provider key to a server you do not control.

items.title: Unshare Public Traces That Are Not Safe to Publish
items.pass: no trace is public unless it was reviewed for publication

console.verify: Tracing > Traces > open the trace > the share control in the header shows the trace as private
console.fix: Tracing > Traces > open the trace > share control > switch Public off

cli.expect: `0`, or only the count of traces on the reviewed publication list. A public trace is readable by anyone holding the link, with no login.

items.title: Enforce Enterprise SSO for Your Verified Domain (Cloud)
items.pass: the corporate domain is verified and its SSO connection is set to Enforced

console.verify: Organization Settings > SSO > the domain shows Verified and the connection shows Enforced
console.fix: Organization Settings > SSO > Verify Domain > add the DNS record shown > Verify; then Configure SSO > enter the IdP details > set Enforced > Save

items.title: Review Audit Logs on a Schedule
items.pass: an owner reviews the organization audit log at least monthly and records the review

console.verify: Organization Settings > Audit Logs > entries since the last recorded review have been read, and the review date is in the security runbook
console.fix: Organization Settings > Audit Logs > read every entry since the last review > record the date and findings in the security runbook > schedule the next review

items.title: Provision and Deprovision Users Through SCIM (point the IdP's SCIM provisioning at /api/public/scim with an organization key; the delete below is the offboarding step)
items.pass: membership is managed by the IdP's SCIM connector and no offboarded person remains in SCIM Users

console.verify: Organization Settings > Members > every member matches an active user in the IdP and nobody who has left is listed
console.fix: Organization Settings > API Keys > Create new API key > Note `idp-scim` > Create; then in the IdP point SCIM provisioning at `$LANGFUSE_HOST/api/public/scim` with that key and assign the Langfuse app to the right groups

cli.expect: `Resources` lists only active employees. A member left behind after offboarding keeps reading traces and prompts.

items.title: Sign Up in the Cloud Data Region Your Residency Policy Allows
items.pass: the organization lives on the region host your residency policy allows and every SDK points at that host

console.verify: Organization Settings > General > the browser address bar shows the allowed region host (`cloud.langfuse.com` for EU, `us.cloud.langfuse.com` for US, `hipaa.cloud.langfuse.com` for HIPAA)
console.fix: `https://<region-host>/auth/sign-up` > create the organization in the allowed region > invite members > repoint every SDK > Organization Settings > General > Delete Organization on the wrong-region organization

cli.expect: the printed host is the allowed region host. Traces sent to another region leave the jurisdiction your policy promised customers.

items.title: Do Not Enable AI Features Until Approved
items.pass: `Enable AI powered features for your organization` is Off unless security approved it

console.verify: Organization Settings > General > AI Features > `Enable AI powered features for your organization` is Off
console.fix: Organization Settings > General > AI Features > switch `Enable AI powered features for your organization` Off > Save

items.title: Turn Off AI Data Use for Product Improvement
items.pass: `AI Data Use for Product/Service Improvement` is Off

console.verify: Organization Settings > General > AI Features > `AI Data Use for Product/Service Improvement` is Off
console.fix: Organization Settings > General > AI Features > switch `AI Data Use for Product/Service Improvement` Off > Save

items.title: Protect the Production Prompt Label
items.pass: `production` and every label an application resolves are protected labels

console.verify: Project Settings > Protected Prompt Labels > the list contains `production` and every label applications resolve
console.fix: Project Settings > Protected Prompt Labels > Add label > `production` > Save; repeat for every label applications resolve

items.title: Disconnect Any Slack Workspace You Do Not Control
items.pass: the Slack integration is disconnected or connected only to your own workspace

console.verify: Project Settings > Integrations > Slack > shows Not connected or the name of your own workspace
console.fix: Project Settings > Integrations > Slack > Disconnect > confirm

items.title: Review and Remove Unnecessary or Unrecognized Integrations
items.pass: every integration (Slack, PostHog, blob storage export) is one your team set up on purpose

console.verify: Project Settings > Integrations > each integration shows Not connected or a destination your team owns
console.fix: Project Settings > Integrations > open the integration > Disconnect or Delete > confirm

cli.expect: `data` lists only exports to buckets you own. An export to a foreign bucket copies every trace out of the project on a schedule.

items.title: Send Webhook Credentials in Headers, Never in the URL
items.pass: every prompt automation webhook carries its token in a header and its URL has no secret in the query string

console.verify: Prompts > Automations > open each webhook > the URL contains no token or key and Headers holds `Authorization: Bearer <receiver-token>`
console.fix: Prompts > Automations > open the webhook > Edit > remove the secret from the URL > Headers > add `Authorization` with the bearer token > Save

items.title: Generate a Unique NEXTAUTH_SECRET, SALT and ENCRYPTION_KEY per Environment at Install (rotating SALT breaks every API key; rotating ENCRYPTION_KEY makes stored credentials unreadable)
items.pass: each environment has its own random `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`, `SALT` and 64-hex-character `ENCRYPTION_KEY`

verify:
kubectl exec deployment/langfuse-web -n $NS -- sh -c \
  'for v in ENCRYPTION_KEY SALT NEXTAUTH_SECRET; do printf "%s=" $v; printenv $v | tr -d "\n" | wc -c; done'
fix:
helm install langfuse langfuse/langfuse -n $NS \
  --set langfuse.salt.value=$(openssl rand -base64 32) \
  --set langfuse.encryptionKey.value=$(openssl rand -hex 32) \
  --set langfuse.nextauth.secret.value=$(openssl rand -base64 32)
cli.expect: `ENCRYPTION_KEY=64` and at least `32` for the other two, with values that differ from every other environment. A shared or default secret lets a leak in staging forge sessions and decrypt credentials in production.

items.title: Remove the Bootstrap Secrets After First Start (the init values are applied once; afterwards they only sit in the environment as live secrets)
items.pass: no `LANGFUSE_INIT_USER_PASSWORD`, `LANGFUSE_INIT_PROJECT_SECRET_KEY` or `LANGFUSE_INIT_PROJECT_PUBLIC_KEY` is set on web or worker

fix:
kubectl set env deployment/langfuse-web deployment/langfuse-worker -n $NS \
  LANGFUSE_INIT_USER_PASSWORD- LANGFUSE_INIT_PROJECT_SECRET_KEY- LANGFUSE_INIT_PROJECT_PUBLIC_KEY-
cli.expect: no output. The init password and project keys stay valid credentials for as long as they sit in the environment.

items.title: Set Data Retention at Provisioning
items.pass: `LANGFUSE_INIT_PROJECT_RETENTION` is set to the day count your policy allows and the bootstrap project shows that retention

console.verify: Project Settings > General > Data Retention shows the day count your policy allows
console.fix: Project Settings > General > Data Retention > enter the number of days > Save

fix: kubectl set env deployment/langfuse-web deployment/langfuse-worker -n $NS LANGFUSE_INIT_PROJECT_RETENTION=<days>
cli.expect: the variable prints the allowed day count and the project's `retentionDays` matches it. A project created without retention keeps every trace until someone remembers to set it.

items.title: Disable Open Sign-Up
items.pass: `AUTH_DISABLE_SIGNUP` is `true` on the web deployment

cli.expect: `true`. With sign-up open, anyone who can reach the host creates an account and, if organization creation is unrestricted, an organization.

items.title: Disable Email/Password When SSO Covers Everyone
items.pass: `AUTH_DISABLE_USERNAME_PASSWORD` is `true` once every user signs in through SSO

cli.expect: `true`. A password login left beside SSO bypasses the IdP's MFA and offboarding.

items.title: Force SSO for Corporate Domains
items.pass: `AUTH_DOMAINS_WITH_SSO_ENFORCEMENT` lists every corporate email domain

cli.expect: a comma-separated list containing every corporate domain. A corporate address that can still log in with a password sidesteps the IdP.

items.title: Require Email Verification Where Password Auth Remains
items.pass: `AUTH_EMAIL_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED` is `true` wherever password login is still enabled

cli.expect: `true`. Without verification an attacker registers with a colleague's address and receives invitations meant for them.

items.title: Shorten the Session Lifetime
items.pass: `AUTH_SESSION_MAX_AGE` is set to the number of minutes your policy allows

cli.expect: the number of minutes your policy allows, not empty. The shipped default is 14 days, so a stolen cookie works for two weeks.

items.title: Do Not Enable Account Linking Unless the IdP Verifies Emails
items.pass: no `AUTH_<PROVIDER>_ALLOW_ACCOUNT_LINKING` is `true` for a provider that does not verify email addresses

cli.expect: no output, or `true` only for providers that verify email. Linking on an unverified email lets a new IdP account take over an existing user by matching their address.

items.title: Pin the SSO Issuer
items.pass: every configured SSO provider has `AUTH_<PROVIDER>_ISSUER` set to your IdP's issuer URL

cli.expect: one line per provider, each ending in your own issuer URL. Without a pinned issuer a token from any tenant of the same IdP product is accepted.

items.title: Set Explicit OAuth Checks on Every SSO Provider
items.pass: every configured SSO provider has `AUTH_<PROVIDER>_CHECKS=pkce,state`

cli.expect: one line per provider, each set to `pkce,state`. Without PKCE and state the authorization code can be intercepted or replayed.

items.title: Limit Google Sign-In to Corporate Domains
items.pass: `AUTH_GOOGLE_ALLOWED_DOMAINS` lists only your corporate domains when Google sign-in is enabled

cli.expect: a comma-separated list of your corporate domains. Without it any Google account, personal ones included, can sign in.

items.title: Restrict Who Can Create Organizations
items.pass: `LANGFUSE_ALLOWED_ORGANIZATION_CREATORS` lists only the owners' addresses

cli.expect: a comma-separated list of owner addresses. Otherwise every user can create organizations and become an owner of their own.

items.title: Set the Auto-Provisioned Default Roles to VIEWER
items.pass: `LANGFUSE_DEFAULT_ORG_ROLE` and `LANGFUSE_DEFAULT_PROJECT_ROLE` are `VIEWER`

fix: kubectl set env deployment/langfuse-web -n $NS LANGFUSE_DEFAULT_ORG_ROLE=VIEWER LANGFUSE_DEFAULT_PROJECT_ROLE=VIEWER
cli.expect: both `LANGFUSE_DEFAULT_ORG_ROLE=VIEWER` and `LANGFUSE_DEFAULT_PROJECT_ROLE=VIEWER`. A higher default hands every auto-provisioned SSO user write access on day one.

items.title: Set a Server-Side Masking Callback
items.pass: `LANGFUSE_INGESTION_MASKING_CALLBACK_URL` points at your masking service on both web and worker

cli.expect: `https://<masking-service>/mask`. Without server-side masking, every SDK that forgets client-side masking writes raw PII into traces.

items.title: Set Masking to Fail Closed
items.pass: `LANGFUSE_INGESTION_MASKING_CALLBACK_FAIL_CLOSED` is `true` on both web and worker

cli.expect: `true`. Failing open stores unmasked events whenever the masking service is down.

items.title: Close the Legacy Ingestion Endpoint
items.pass: `LANGFUSE_MIGRATION_V4_WRITE_MODE` is unset once every SDK is on the current ingestion path

fix: kubectl set env deployment/langfuse-web deployment/langfuse-worker -n $NS LANGFUSE_MIGRATION_V4_WRITE_MODE-
cli.expect: no output. The legacy write path skips the masking callback and keeps a second, unhardened way to write traces.

items.title: Enforce HTTPS at the CSP Layer
items.pass: `LANGFUSE_CSP_ENFORCE_HTTPS` is `true` on the web deployment

cli.expect: `true`. Without it a page loaded over plain HTTP sends session cookies in clear text.

items.title: Turn Off Telemetry (OSS)
items.pass: `TELEMETRY_ENABLED` is `false` on web and worker

fix: kubectl set env deployment/langfuse-web deployment/langfuse-worker -n $NS TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false
cli.expect: `false`. Telemetry reports usage from your instance to a third party your data policy may not cover.

items.title: Do Not Set SSRF Allowlists Unless an Internal Target Is Required
items.pass: no `LANGFUSE_*WHITELISTED*` variable is set unless a documented internal target needs it

items.title: Never Run Code Evaluators In-Process
items.pass: `LANGFUSE_CODE_EVAL_DISPATCHER` is unset or set to a sandboxed dispatcher

fix: kubectl set env deployment/langfuse-web deployment/langfuse-worker -n $NS LANGFUSE_CODE_EVAL_DISPATCHER-
cli.expect: no output, or a sandboxed dispatcher named in your runbook. An in-process evaluator runs user-authored code inside the Langfuse container with its secrets.

items.title: Generate a High-Entropy Admin API Key and Do Not Expose the Admin API Publicly
items.pass: `ADMIN_API_KEY` is at least 64 random characters and `/api/admin` is blocked at the ingress

verify: kubectl exec deployment/langfuse-web -n $NS -- printenv ADMIN_API_KEY | tr -d '\n' | wc -c
fix:
kubectl create secret generic langfuse-admin -n $NS --from-literal=ADMIN_API_KEY=$(openssl rand -base64 48) && \
  kubectl set env deployment/langfuse-web -n $NS --from=secret/langfuse-admin
cli.expect: a length of at least `64`, and `403` or `404` from outside the network rather than `401`. A guessable or reachable admin key controls every organization on the instance.

items.title: Sandbox or Disable the Assistant's Code Tools (or set LANGFUSE_IN_APP_AGENT_ENABLED=false)
items.pass: the in-app agent is disabled, or its sandbox provider is `lambda-microvm` with image, role, region and egress connector set

fix: kubectl set env deployment/langfuse-web deployment/langfuse-worker -n $NS LANGFUSE_IN_APP_AGENT_ENABLED=false
cli.expect: `LANGFUSE_IN_APP_AGENT_ENABLED=false`, or `LANGFUSE_IN_APP_AGENT_SANDBOX_PROVIDER=lambda-microvm` together with the image, execution role, region and egress connector variables. Unsandboxed code tools run model-written code inside the application.

items.title: Expose Only the Web Container
items.pass: `langfuse-web` is the only Service of type `LoadBalancer` or `NodePort` in the namespace

cli.expect: every Service except `langfuse-web` shows `ClusterIP`. An exposed worker, Postgres, ClickHouse, Redis or MinIO is reachable without any Langfuse authentication.

items.title: Enable Encryption at Rest on Every Store
items.pass: every bucket Langfuse writes to has default SSE-KMS encryption, and the database volumes are encrypted

console.verify: S3 > Buckets > `<event-upload-bucket>` > Properties > Default encryption shows `SSE-KMS` with your key; repeat for the media and export buckets
console.fix: S3 > Buckets > `<event-upload-bucket>` > Properties > Default encryption > Edit > `SSE-KMS` > choose the key > Save changes

cli.expect: `SSEAlgorithm` is `aws:kms` with your `KMSMasterKeyID`. Unencrypted buckets hand every raw event and media upload to whoever obtains the storage credentials.

items.title: Grant the Retention Job Delete Rights on Every Bucket
items.pass: the Langfuse role can `s3:DeleteObject` on the event, media and export buckets

console.verify: IAM > Roles > `<langfuse-role>` > Permissions > a policy allows `s3:DeleteObject` on every bucket Langfuse writes to
console.fix: IAM > Roles > `<langfuse-role>` > Permissions > Add permissions > Create inline policy > JSON > allow `s3:DeleteObject` on `arn:aws:s3:::<media-bucket>/*` and the other buckets > Next > name `LangfuseRetentionDelete` > Create policy

verify:
aws iam simulate-principal-policy --policy-source-arn <langfuse-role-arn> --action-names s3:DeleteObject \
  --resource-arns arn:aws:s3:::<media-bucket>/* --query 'EvaluationResults[].EvalDecision' --output text
cli.expect: `allowed`. Without delete rights the retention job silently leaves expired traces and media in the buckets.

items.title: Upgrade the Instance to the Latest Release
items.pass: web and worker run the image tag of the latest Langfuse release

fix: helm repo update && helm upgrade langfuse langfuse/langfuse -n $NS --reuse-values
cli.expect: the running image tag equals the chart's current `app_version`. An old release misses security fixes that are public in the changelog.

guides.title: Ledger Configuration
checklistItems: Purchase devices directly from ledger.com only — never from marketplaces, resellers, or second-hand sources
Inspect packaging on arrival and reject any device that arrives with a pre-filled recovery sheet, included instructions to use a specific seed, or signs of tampering
Ledger Live > My Ledger > Run Genuine check to cryptographically verify the device before first use
Generate the recovery seed on the device itself — never accept, type in, or restore a seed provided by anyone else
Set a strong PIN (8 digits) that is not reused elsewhere; be aware the device wipes itself after 3 incorrect PIN attempts
Update firmware only through Ledger Live — never from links in emails, chats, or pop-ups
Review the official release notes before applying a firmware update
My Ledger > App catalog > Install only the apps you actually need; uninstall unused apps (keys are unaffected by app removal)
Settings (on device) > Security > Passphrase (25th word) > Enable for high-value accounts; store the passphrase separately from the seed in a password manager
Settings (on device) > Security > Auto-lock > Set a short timeout (e.g. 1–5 minutes)
Settings (on device) > Security > PIN lock > Require PIN entry whenever the device is connected
Keep Blind signing OFF by default in each app's settings — enable only per-session when a specific interaction explicitly requires it, and disable immediately afterwards
Verify the full recipient address and amount on the device screen before approving — never trust only what the computer or dApp displays
Prefer clear signing with compatible apps and dApps so the device shows human-readable transaction details
Download Ledger Live only from ledger.com — never from ads, search results, or third-party stores
Verify the installer (checksum/signature published by Ledger) before running it
Never install browser extensions claiming to be "Ledger" — Ledger does not distribute a wallet browser extension
Settings > Help > Analytics / usage data > Disable (optional, reduces data exposure)
Back up the seed on a steel/metal backup plate resistant to fire and water
Never digitize the seed — no photos, cloud notes, password managers, email drafts, or text files
Decline Ledger Recover unless your organization's policy explicitly accepts the custodial-shard tradeoffs — document the decision either way
Test recovery by restoring the seed on a spare device, then wiping it, to confirm the backup is correct
Remember: Ledger will never ask for your 24-word recovery phrase — anyone who does is an attacker

Treat "security update", "wallet migration", or "data breach compensation" emails as phishing — Ledger customer data leaks make such lures common; navigate to ledger.com manually instead of clicking links

Rotate the Master Key on a Schedule by Replacing the Secret (with a salt key set, never through /key/regenerate) - pass: the master key Secret was replaced inside your rotation window and the previous value is refused
Do Not Return the Master Key to Admin UI Sessions - pass: general_settings.disable_master_key_return is true
Create a Personal Proxy Admin Account for Every Administrator - pass: every administrator has a proxy_admin user with their own email, and the shared environment login is used for recovery only

Restrict Admin UI SSO Sign-In to Admin Roles - pass: general_settings.ui_access_mode is admin_only

Sign Admins In Through Your Identity Provider (free for up to five user records; beyond that a licence) - pass: /sso/readiness reports the provider configured with its pinned endpoints, PROXY_BASE_URL is your public URL, and SSO_ENABLED is true
Restrict SSO Sign-In to Corporate Email Domains - pass: ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS lists every corporate domain and nothing else
Bind the Proxy Admin Role to One SSO Identity - pass: PROXY_ADMIN_ID is set to the administrator's identity-provider user id

Restrict Who May Create Virtual Keys - pass: litellm_settings.key_generation_settings limits team keys to team admins and personal keys to proxy admins

Allowlist Models on Every Virtual Key - pass: every key's models names the deployments the workload needs; no key has an empty list or a catch-all entry (*, all-proxy-models, all-team-models)

Allowlist Models on Every Team - pass: every team's models names its approved deployments; no team has an empty list or a catch-all entry (all-proxy-models, *)
Set a Per-Member Budget on Every Team (member key lifetime is licence-gated) - pass: every team's member budget carries a cap and a reset window
Do Not Auto-Add the Creating Admin to Every Team - pass: general_settings.disable_auto_add_proxy_admin_to_teams is true
Cap What Any Virtual Key Can Be Created With - pass: litellm_settings.upperbound_key_generate_params sets a maximum budget, duration and rate limit for every key

Set a Budget With a Reset Window and Rate Limits on Every Team - pass: every team has max_budget, budget_duration, rpm_limit and tpm_limit set
Set a Proxy-Wide Budget Ceiling - pass: litellm_settings.max_budget and budget_duration are set and /global/spend reports the cap
Enforce Budgets Against the Database (fail closed) - pass: general_settings.fail_closed_budget_enforcement is true
Require an End-User Identifier on Every Request - pass: general_settings.enforce_user_param is true

Set a Default Budget for End Users - pass: a budget object exists and litellm_settings.max_end_user_budget_id names it

Do Not Expose Wildcard Models (a entry routes any model name straight to the provider account) - pass: no model_list entry has a anywhere in its litellm_params.model

Do Not Enable Client-Side Credentials (a request body could then point the proxy's provider key at a caller-chosen host) - pass: general_settings.allow_client_side_credentials is unset or false and no model sets configurable_clientside_auth_params

items.title: Set a Master Key From a Secret (never run the proxy without one)
items.pass: the master key reaches the proxy from a Kubernetes Secret (`PROXY_MASTER_KEY` on the chart's Deployment, read by `general_settings.master_key`) as `sk-` plus at least 32 random characters, and an unauthenticated request is refused

verify:
kubectl get configmap litellm-config -n $NS -o jsonpath='{.data.config\.yaml}' \
  | yq '.general_settings.master_key'
kubectl exec deployment/litellm -n $NS -- sh -c 'printenv PROXY_MASTER_KEY | tr -d "\n" | wc -c'
fix:
yq -i 'del(.masterkey) | .proxy_config.general_settings.master_key = "os.environ/PROXY_MASTER_KEY"' values.yaml \
  && helm upgrade litellm oci://ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-helm -n $NS -f values.yaml \
  && REF=$(kubectl get deployment litellm -n $NS -o jsonpath='{range .spec.template.spec.containers[0].env[?(@.name=="PROXY_MASTER_KEY")]}{.valueFrom.secretKeyRef.name}/{.valueFrom.secretKeyRef.key}{end}') \
  && kubectl patch secret "${REF%/*}" -n $NS -p "{\"stringData\":{\"${REF#*/}\":\"sk-$(openssl rand -hex 32)\"}}" \
  && kubectl rollout restart deployment/litellm -n $NS
cli.expect: `401` from the first command, `os.environ/PROXY_MASTER_KEY` from the second and at least `35` from the third. With no master key every caller is an internal user who can call models, mint keys and reset spend.

items.title: Set a Dedicated Salt Key Before the First Credential Is Stored
items.pass: `LITELLM_SALT_KEY` is set from a Kubernetes Secret and differs from the master key

verify: kubectl exec deployment/litellm -n $NS -- sh -c 'printenv LITELLM_SALT_KEY | tr -d "\n" | wc -c'
kubectl exec deployment/litellm -n $NS -- sh -c '[ "$LITELLM_SALT_KEY" != "$PROXY_MASTER_KEY" ] && echo differs || echo same-as-master'
fix:
kubectl create secret generic litellm-salt -n $NS --from-literal=LITELLM_SALT_KEY=sk-$(openssl rand -hex 32) \
  && kubectl set env deployment/litellm -n $NS --from=secret/litellm-salt
cli.expect: at least `35` (the `sk-` prefix plus 32 characters) from the first command and `differs` from the second. Otherwise the master key encrypts every stored provider credential, so replacing its Secret breaks them - and so does adding the salt once credentials are stored, until each one is re-entered.

items.title: Connect a Managed Postgres Key Store Over Verified TLS
items.pass: `DATABASE_URL` points at your managed Postgres with `sslmode=verify-full`, and `/health/readiness` reports `db` as `connected`

verify: kubectl exec deployment/litellm -n $NS -- sh -c 'printenv DATABASE_URL | grep -o "sslmode=[a-z-]*"'
fix:
kubectl create secret generic litellm-db -n $NS --from-literal=username=<db-user> --from-literal=password=<db-password> \
  && kubectl create secret generic litellm-db-ca -n $NS --from-file=ca.pem=<ca-bundle.pem> \
  && yq -i '.db.useExisting = true | .db.deployStandalone = false | .db.endpoint = "<db-host>" | .db.database = "<db-name>" | .db.secret.name = "litellm-db"' values.yaml \
  && yq -i '.db.url = "postgresql://$(DATABASE_USERNAME):$(DATABASE_PASSWORD)@$(DATABASE_HOST)/$(DATABASE_NAME)?sslmode=verify-full&sslrootcert=/certs/ca.pem"' values.yaml \
  && yq -i '.volumes = ([.volumes[] | select(.name != "db-ca")] + [{"name": "db-ca", "secret": {"secretName": "litellm-db-ca"}}])' values.yaml \
  && yq -i '.volumeMounts = ([.volumeMounts[] | select(.name != "db-ca")] + [{"name": "db-ca", "mountPath": "/certs", "readOnly": true}])' values.yaml \
  && helm upgrade litellm oci://ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-helm -n $NS -f values.yaml
cli.expect: `"db":"connected"` and `sslmode=verify-full`. A missing database means no key store and no enforced budgets; an unverified connection exposes every hashed key and credential in transit.

items.title: Rotate the Master Key on a Schedule by Replacing the Secret (with a salt key set, never through /key/regenerate)
items.pass: the master key Secret was replaced inside your rotation window and the previous value is refused

fix:
kubectl create secret generic litellm-masterkey -n $NS --from-literal=masterkey=sk-$(openssl rand -hex 32) \
  --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f - && kubectl rollout restart deployment/litellm -n $NS
cli.expect: `401` for the previous value and a Secret timestamp inside your rotation window. A master key that never rotates keeps every past leak live.

items.title: Do Not Return the Master Key to Admin UI Sessions
items.pass: `general_settings.disable_master_key_return` is `true`

verify:
kubectl get configmap litellm-config -n $NS -o jsonpath='{.data.config\.yaml}' \
  | yq '.general_settings.disable_master_key_return'
fix:
yq -i '.proxy_config.general_settings.disable_master_key_return = true' values.yaml \
  && helm upgrade litellm oci://ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-helm -n $NS -f values.yaml
cli.expect: `true`. With it off, the bootstrap admin's dashboard session lists the master key's own token record whenever one exists in the key table.

items.title: Create a Personal Proxy Admin Account for Every Administrator
items.pass: every administrator has a `proxy_admin` user with their own email, and the shared environment login is used for recovery only

console.verify: Admin UI > Internal Users > Users > Global Proxy Role column shows `Admin (All Permissions)` for each named administrator, not only for `default_user_id`
console.fix: Admin UI > Internal Users > + Invite User > User Email > Global Proxy Role `Admin (All Permissions)` > tick `Send invitation email` only if SSO is off > Invite User

cli.expect: one email per administrator, plus one `null` line for the environment login's `default_user_id`. A shared bootstrap login cannot be rotated per person or revoked for a single leaver. Once SSO is on, leave `Send invitation email` unticked and set `send_invite_email` to `false`: the emailed link sets a password and opens an admin session outside SSO for about a week, while the new administrator can sign in through the identity provider instead.

items.title: Set a UI Username and a UI Password That Is Not the Master Key
items.pass: `UI_USERNAME` is not `admin` and `UI_PASSWORD` is set from a Secret to a value that differs from the master key

verify: kubectl exec deployment/litellm -n $NS -- sh -c '[ "${UI_USERNAME:-admin}" != admin ] && [ -n "$UI_PASSWORD" ] && echo set || echo default'
fix:
kubectl create secret generic litellm-ui-login -n $NS --from-literal=UI_USERNAME=<ui-username> \
  --from-literal=UI_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -base64 24) && kubectl set env deployment/litellm -n $NS --from=secret/litellm-ui-login
cli.expect: `set` from the first command and `401` from the login, or `403` once password login is turned off beside SSO. Without them the default `admin` login with the API root key is a guessable takeover of both the UI and the API.

items.title: Shorten the Admin UI Session Lifetime
items.pass: `LITELLM_UI_SESSION_DURATION` is set to the hours your policy allows, not the 24-hour default

cli.expect: a duration shorter than `24h`, such as `8h`. The default keeps a stolen admin session cookie valid for a day.

items.title: Restrict Admin UI SSO Sign-In to Admin Roles
items.pass: `general_settings.ui_access_mode` is `admin_only`

verify:
kubectl get configmap litellm-config -n $NS -o jsonpath='{.data.config\.yaml}' \
  | yq '.general_settings.ui_access_mode'
fix:
yq -i '.proxy_config.general_settings.ui_access_mode = "admin_only"' values.yaml \
  && helm upgrade litellm oci://ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-helm -n $NS -f values.yaml

  && helm upgrade litellm oci://ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-helm -n $NS -f values.yaml
cli.expect: no output from either command. A stdio server is a command the proxy spawns in its own container as the proxy's user, with the container's files and network reach.

items.title: Limit Request Body Size at the Ingress (the proxy's own size limit is licence-gated)
items.pass: the ingress in front of the proxy caps request bodies, and `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-body-size` is not `0`

fix:
yq -i '.ingress.annotations."nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-body-size" = "<body-size>"' values.yaml \
  && helm upgrade litellm oci://ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-helm -n $NS -f values.yaml
cli.expect: `litellm` and a bounded size such as `10m`, or `litellm` and an empty second field where the controller's own `1m` default applies; never `0`, and never `NotFound` - an ingress that does not exist caps nothing at all, and the item that terminates TLS in front of the proxy is what creates it. A limit of `0` turns the body-size check off, and one caller can then push multi-megabyte prompts through the tokenizer and the provider on every request.

items.title: Terminate TLS in Front of the Proxy and Enable HSTS
items.pass: the proxy is reachable only through an HTTPS ingress bound to its host name, `PROXY_BASE_URL` is `https://<litellm-host>` and `LITELLM_ENABLE_HSTS` is `true`

fix:
yq -i '.ingress.enabled = true | .ingress.hosts[0].host = "<litellm-host>" | .ingress.hosts[0].paths[0].path = "/" | .ingress.hosts[0].paths[0].pathType = "Prefix" | .ingress.tls[0].secretName = "<tls-secret>" | .ingress.tls[0].hosts[0] = "<litellm-host>" | .envVars.PROXY_BASE_URL = "https://<litellm-host>" | .envVars.LITELLM_ENABLE_HSTS = "true"' values.yaml \
  && helm upgrade litellm oci://ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-helm -n $NS -f values.yaml
cli.expect: a `strict-transport-security` header, your host under `tls`, `https://<litellm-host>` from the third command and `true` from the fourth (an ingress controller can add the header on its own; the fourth command reads the proxy's own switch). Otherwise bearer keys and prompts cross the network in clear text, and the proxy, which sees only the plain-HTTP hop behind the ingress, issues the Admin UI session cookie without `Secure`.

items.title: Restrict CORS to Named Origins
items.pass: `LITELLM_CORS_ORIGINS` lists your application origins and a foreign origin gets no `access-control-allow-origin`

cli.expect: no output; never `*` or the foreign origin echoed back. A wildcard lets any web page drive the proxy from a visitor's browser.

items.title: Turn Off the Swagger, ReDoc and OpenAPI Pages (they answer without a key and list every management route)
items.pass: `NO_DOCS`, `NO_REDOC` and `NO_OPENAPI` are `True` and `/openapi.json` returns `404`

fix: kubectl set env deployment/litellm -n $NS NO_DOCS=True NO_REDOC=True NO_OPENAPI=True
cli.expect: `404`. The default serves the full route schema and a request form to anyone who can reach the port. `/routes` still lists every path, pass-through endpoints included, without a key and has no switch - block it at the ingress.

items.title: Serve Only the Inference Routes on Application-Facing Replicas
items.pass: the application-facing release sets `general_settings.allowed_routes` to the inference and health routes, and a management route on its host name answers `403`

fix:
cp values.yaml values-app.yaml \
  && yq -i '.proxy_config.general_settings.allowed_routes = ["/v1/chat/completions", "/chat/completions", "/v1/embeddings", "/embeddings", "/v1/models", "/models", "/health/liveliness", "/health/readiness"] | .ingress.enabled = true | .ingress.hosts[0].host = "<app-host>" | .ingress.hosts[0].paths[0].path = "/" | .ingress.hosts[0].paths[0].pathType = "Prefix" | .ingress.tls[0].hosts[0] = "<app-host>" | .ingress.tls[0].secretName = "<app-tls-secret>" | .masterkeySecretName = "litellm-masterkey" | .masterkeySecretKey = "masterkey"' values-app.yaml \
  && helm upgrade --install litellm-app oci://ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-helm -n $NS -f values-app.yaml
cli.expect: `403` from the application host name, while your own applications still get `200`. The list is a template and the comparison is an exact string match on the request path, so a route your applications call and you did not list - `/v1/responses`, `/v1/messages`, `/moderations`, `/rerank` - loses production traffic. The list is checked only on routes that take a key, so `/login`, `/v2/login`, `/onboarding/*`, the `/ui` bundle and `/get/ui_settings` still answer on the application host - block those paths at the ingress as well. A public replica that also serves /key, /team and /login turns any key leak into gateway administration.

items.title: Disable the Admin UI on Application-Facing Replicas
items.pass: `DISABLE_ADMIN_UI` is `True` on the application-facing release and its host name's `/litellm/.well-known/litellm-ui-config` reports `admin_ui_disabled` as `true`, while the `litellm` release you administer from reports `false`

fix:
yq -i '.envVars.DISABLE_ADMIN_UI = "True"' values-app.yaml \
  && helm upgrade --install litellm-app oci://ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-helm -n $NS -f values-app.yaml
cli.expect: `true` from the first command and `false` from the second. The variable only hides the UI: `POST /login` still issues an admin session cookie, so a public replica that answers `/login` is still a password-login surface. On the release you administer from it would also switch off the SSO sign-in, so keep it out of `values.yaml`; the Fix writes it to `values-app.yaml`, which the item before this one creates.

items.title: Restrict Which Namespaces Can Reach the Proxy (the proxy's own IP allowlist is licence-gated)
items.pass: a NetworkPolicy selects the proxy pods and admits only the ingress controller and the application namespaces

fix:
kubectl apply -n $NS -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: litellm-ingress
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: litellm
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
  ingress:
    - from:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: <ingress-namespace>
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: <application-namespace>
      ports:
        - port: 4000
EOF
cli.expect: a line whose selector is the proxy's own (`app.kubernetes.io/name`: `litellm`), whose `types` include `Ingress`, and in which every rule carries a `from` naming your ingress and application namespaces. A rule with no `from`, such as `[{}]`, admits every pod in the cluster, which is the state this item exists to remove; `ingress=` with nothing after it denies all ingress only when `types` include `Ingress` - an `Egress`-only policy restricts nothing on the way in.

items.title: Do Not Turn Off Authentication on the Metrics Endpoint

kubectl get deploy litellm -n $NS -o jsonpath='{range .spec.template.spec.containers[0].env[?(@.value)]}{.name}{"\n"}{end}' | grep -E '^REDIS_(URL|PASSWORD)$'

kubectl get configmap litellm-config -n $NS -o jsonpath='{.data.config\.yaml}' \
  | yq '[.general_settings.coordination_redis, .litellm_settings.cache_params]'
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" $LITELLM_HOST/coordination_redis/settings | jq -c '{source, ssl: .values.ssl, password_set: (.values.password != null), url_set: (.values.url != null)}'
fix:
kubectl create secret generic litellm-redis -n $NS --from-literal=REDIS_PASSWORD=<redis-password> --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f - \

cli.expect: `rediss` and `password` from the first command, or `no-password` alone from the first and all three variable names and `true` from the second; nothing from the third, which names a password or url written as a literal `value:`; two `null`s from the fourth unless the block names the same TLS endpoint; and from the fifth a `source` that is the store you configured, with `ssl` and `password_set` true - or `url_set` true for a `rediss` url that carries the password - when it is `coordination_redis`. A `REDIS_URL` from a Secret under `environmentSecrets:` outranks `REDIS_HOST`, so delete it from that Secret; `REDIS_URL-` removes only a literal entry.
